parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the Python argparse, bech32 convertbits, ESM .mjs, no npm dependencies, /output placement, Python list formatting, direct executable probing, and no Uint8Array/DataView requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After initial executable probes, the parent split the work into two children: agent-0 owned convertbits.mjs and pyformat.mjs, agent-1 owned argparse.mjs and test14.mjs, while the parent retained final integration verification.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 implemented arithmetic convertbits and formatPyList. Agent-1 implemented an argparse clone, Python-like int parsing including underscores, traceback-like error handling, and the test14.mjs entry using the agreed imports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The children wrote disjoint files in /output. Agent-1 observed the library files before end-to-end runs, and the parent later read all four delivered files before closing.
parallel.verification: Agent-0 ran module assertions. Agent-1 ran node --check, two sample runs, and a 22-case differential harness. The parent ran additional sample and edge comparisons plus two argparse error checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Agent-1 explicitly reported a remaining negative --b/--c/--d divergence; the parent did not test or fix that reported issue. The official completed evaluation still failed 2 of 32 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same porting requirements, including ESM modules, manual argv parsing, Python list formatting, executable probing, and no external dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single actor owned all work directly, first probing reference behavior, then writing the conversion helper, int parser, argparse-like parser, formatter, and entry file itself.
serial.implementation: The serial solution used a bitwise convertbits implementation, a pyInt helper, argparser.mjs, pyformat.mjs exporting pyListRepr, and a test14.mjs entry that printed the two conversion outputs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were written by the same actor and imported by the entry file. The final artifact contained test14.mjs and four library files.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran the four sample cases, edge cases for missing/invalid arguments and invalid data, and a 60-case random valid-input fuzz comparison against the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial actor noted negative bit-size behavior as probably rare and did not fully implement that path; the official completed evaluation failed 2 of 32 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM port, CLI parity, output formatting, no dependencies, and executable probing, and child agent-1 additionally probed underscored integer behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same core requirements and tested samples plus several argparse and invalid-data paths in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the visible task obligations, but parallel distributed requirement discovery across children and surfaced a child-reported negative bit-size gap; serial kept the gap as a local implementation limitation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a two-child split: one child owned convertbits and formatting, another owned argparse and the entry file, with the parent responsible for final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor own probing, all module writes, entry integration, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had clear component ownership and a parent integration role; serial avoided inter-agent ownership boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts gave disjoint file scopes and an explicit import contract between the entry file and the library files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local module names and imports under one actor, so no cross-agent interface handoff was needed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The cross-agent interface itself was specified and worked, but the parallel parent had to consume a large aggregate handoff containing a known divergence, which serial did not have.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final code used arithmetic masking in convertbits and a more detailed argparse.mjs with pyIntParse, pyRepr, traceback handling, and direct imports in test14.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final code used a bitwise convertbits module, pyint.mjs, argparser.mjs, pyformat.mjs, and a simpler test14.mjs entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel improved the convertbits arithmetic implementation relative to serial's bitwise path, while serial used a simpler module split and also missed negative bit-size behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both child results returned to the parent in the AgentSwarm aggregate, including the CLI child's explicit known divergence note.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; local observations and files remained in one actor's context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an actionable child finding at the handoff boundary that the parent did not carry into final verification, while serial had no such handoff to consume.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote in the same /output tree but under disjoint file ownership, and child agent-1 listed the already-created library files before writing its own parser and entry files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files itself and imported its own local module names without concurrent writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared workspace coordination but no observed file collision; serial had no shared-state coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification included child module assertions, child syntax checks and a 22-case differential harness, parent sample/edge checks, and final file reads; official evaluation still failed 30 of 32.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification included samples, edge cases, and a 60-case valid-input fuzz comparison; official evaluation also failed 30 of 32.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more inter-agent verification artifacts but missed the child-reported negative-bit case; serial performed stronger valid-input fuzzing but did not handle all official cases either.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout but used two subagents, 49 tool calls, about 616k tokens, and 734 agent seconds before closing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout using one actor, 12 tool calls, about 228k tokens, and 211 agent seconds before closing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed far more coordination budget but still had ample time and finished normally; budget pressure was not the observed cause of the shared official failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial are marked solution_passed false with 30 of 32 samples passed. The process difference is still concrete. Parallel delegated library and CLI work to two children and produced a stronger arithmetic convertbits module, but it also received and then failed to act on the CLI child's known negative bit-size divergence. Serial kept all work local, used a bitwise convertbits implementation, and also left negative bit-size behavior incomplete. The official summaries do not expose the two failing cases, so the retained parallel pattern is an adverse process issue rather than a proven exclusive cause of an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Two-child split produced disjoint files and a returned aggregate handoff.
Child agent-1 reported a known negative --b/--c/--d divergence that the parent did not cover in final verification.
Official completed evaluation for the parallel artifact failed 2 of 32 cases.
serial_contributors: Single actor owned all implementation and verification without child handoffs.
Serial valid-input sample and fuzz verification passed locally but did not cover every official hidden behavior.
Official completed evaluation for the serial artifact also failed 2 of 32 cases.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial used bitwise JavaScript operations in convertbits, while parallel used arithmetic masking.
Both attempts appear to leave negative bit-size behavior under-specified or unhandled in local verification.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluator summaries report only 30 of 32 and do not expose which hidden samples failed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process pattern observed, but no pass/fail outcome difference and no exclusive root cause proven
